recentItems.title: Aussie dollar surges against Yen as Japan lifts interest rates | Finance Report | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The Australian dollar rose sharply against the yen as the Bank of Japan lifted interest rates to their highest level in three decades. 
With two dissenters on the BoJ board, the lack of consensus is raising doubts about how committed the Japanese central bank is to hiking rates to curb higher inflation. 
Elsewhere, the Bank of England kept rates on hold, while surging fuel prices as a result of the US-Iran war have led to Donald Trump's approval ratings taking a massive hit. 
The ASX, meanwhile, has dropped almost 4 per cent since the month began. 

Presented by David Chau.

recentItems.title: Sydney woman sentenced to minimum three years' jail over husband's killing | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
A Sydney woman who killed and dismembered her husband has been handed a minimum jail sentence of three years and could be release on parole by October 2027.
Nirmeen Noufl pleaded guilty to the lesser charge of manslaughter just as her Supreme Court murder trial was due to begin.
A judge described the disposal of Mamdouh Noufl's body as "chilling", but he took into account a history of childhood dysfunction and domestic violence in sentencing.

recentItems.title: RBA to lift interest rates two more times, says State Street senior strategist | The Business
recentItems.description:
Major central banks around the world are hiking interest rates as higher energy prices compound inflation problems. Financial markets and most economists think the Reserve Bank of Australia will soon join them on September 29. Financial market predictions of the cash rate rising to 4.6 per cent this month rose as high as 95 per cent on Friday.  Clive Maguchu from State Street told Alicia Barry he has no doubts this will occur.  

He said "we've seen the synchronised move higher by a lot of central banks, looking to act against the rising tide of inflation so we think the RBA will join that tide." 

Clive Maguchu says the RBA won't be done at 4.6 per cent, but he wouldn't put a peak on the cash rate saying the economic environment is too uncertain. 

"We feel there'll be a second hike to follow, but that all depends on the progress on inflation." He said. 

Clive Maguchu also discusses how investors are resetting their expectations around interest rates and what it means for various market sectors. The ASX 200 closed flat at 8,731 on Friday, off 0.1% for the week.
